content.text:
Found it. Commit 3fb5048f introduced the entire `MOUSE_TRANSPARENT` mechanism (setting `previousNode.setMouseTransparent(true)` when switching content, and restoring it via the stored property when the transition finishes). The fix commit removes exactly this mechanism and replaces it with `view.setMouseTransparent(...)` on the whole StackPane instead of on individual nodes.

The bug: `previousNode.getProperties().put(MOUSE_TRANSPARENT, previousNode.isMouseTransparent())` stores the mouse-transparent state on the node that is *about to become* the previous node, at the point content is switched — but by the time the removal callback runs, `previousNode` field may refer to a different node (or the same node's mouse-transparent flag may have already been altered elsewhere / the currentNode itself never gets its transparency reset if it becomes previousNode later without another switch happening in between). Essentially, per-node bookkeeping of a transient "previous mouse transparent state" property doesn't survive rapid/overlapping transitions correctly, causing incorrect mouse-transparency being applied to nodes (blocking mouse input on pages that shouldn't be blocked, or vice versa). The fix commit's own message "fix bug" plus removing that whole property based system in favor of tracking mouse-transparency at the container `view` level (which is unambiguous — only one previous node is inside the view at a time) confirms this was the root design flaw.

The subsequent commit e9db183d isn't the cause — it only wraps the same logic in `Platform.runLater` and preserves the buggy property-restore pattern unchanged, so it inherited but didn't introduce the bug.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 3fb5048f103ed958bdd87207f6b6c929b5ef7eca

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the file history of `TransitionHandler.java` with `git log --follow` and examined each commit's diff in order, looking for when the `setMouseTransparent`/`MOUSE_TRANSPARENT` property logic (which the fix commit removes) was first introduced.

(2) Commit `3fb5048f` ("Fix IllegalStateException in DownloadWizardProvider") introduced the `MOUSE_TRANSPARENT` static property key and the associated logic: when switching views it stashes `previousNode.isMouseTransparent()` into a property on that node and sets `previousNode.setMouseTransparent(true)`; then, when the transition's removal `KeyFrame` fires, it restores the transparency from that stashed property before removing the node. This per-node bookkeeping approach is exactly what commit `2324af64` deletes, replacing it with a much simpler `view.setMouseTransparent(true/false)` applied to the whole StackPane.

(3) The fix commit's diff is a near-exact inverse of `3fb5048f`'s diff (removes the same `MOUSE_TRANSPARENT` field, the `getProperties().put(...)` call, and the `getProperties().get(...)` restore call), and the fix commit message explicitly says "fix bug" referring to this mechanism. The intermediate commit `e9db183d` only wraps the same buggy code in `Platform.runLater` without altering the flawed logic, so it propagated but did not introduce the defect.

I'm fairly confident in this attribution given the diff symmetry, though I did not run the application to reproduce the exact mouse-transparency glitch (e.g., a page unexpectedly blocking/allowing mouse clicks during rapid transitions).
